competencies.name: L1 inference — what the model itself contributes
competencies.decision: when a run fails, was it the model or the thing around it?
competencies.authority_declared: NVIDIA NOOA is the only source here that HOLDS THE MODEL FIXED and varies the harness, which is the one experiment that can answer this question at all

sources.why: same model, double-digit benchmark swing from harness design alone — the measurement that makes L1 and L2 separable rather than a figure of speech
Minimal mode is a two-tool agent (persistent bash + str_replace_editor): a deliberately thin harness, which is the control condition for measuring a model

competencies.name: L2 runtime — who terminates the loop
competencies.decision: the run is going; what stops it, and who owns that decision?
competencies.authority_declared: the four sources DISAGREE, and the disagreement is the lesson: Nygard bounds a callee that never stops, Young reports an agent that stops too eagerly, Anthropic 2024 offers a max-iteration cap, DeepSeek makes the loop a swappable plugin

sources.why: the caller-side Timeout and the Circuit Breaker: termination imposed from outside because the callee will never do it
the documented failure runs the OTHER way — the agent declares victory early — and the fix is a completion predicate the agent does not own
states the plain fallback: stopping conditions such as a maximum number of iterations, to maintain control
loops are listed as a plugin alongside models and tools, so termination becomes a configuration choice rather than a property of the model

competencies.name: L2 runtime — framework versus harness
competencies.decision: adopt a framework, or build the harness thin and keep the seams?
competencies.authority_declared: Anthropic argues down from abstraction; DeepSeek and NVIDIA both argue for an inspectable substrate, one via plugins and one via plain Python — three practitioner answers, not one

sources.why: frameworks 'often create extra layers of abstraction that can obscure the underlying prompts and responses, making them harder to debug'
AGENT = MODEL + HARNESS, stated as an identity, with every capability swappable in configuration
collapses the boundary into syntax: a method body of `...` is completed by an LLM loop, a normal body runs as deterministic Python

sources.$note: `verified` is not decoration. It is the receipt that this row was read rather than recalled, and it is what CF-026 exists to force.

nvidia-noaa-harness.title: Six Agent Harness Capabilities for Higher Model Performance (NVIDIA Labs Object-Oriented Agents, NOOA)
nvidia-noaa-harness.author: Ricardo Silveira Cabral and Paul Furgale, distinguished research scientists, NVIDIA
nvidia-noaa-harness.audience: ICP1 and ICP2 both — it is the only source that prices harness design in benchmark points AND in tokens, which is the pair of currencies the two readers each care about separately
nvidia-noaa-harness.ranking_criterion: it runs the controlled experiment: the model is held fixed and the harness is varied, and the swing is reported in both score and token cost. Every other source here asserts that the harness matters; this one measures how much.
nvidia-noaa-harness.acquisition: read in the browser 2026-08-26; not ingested into a cartridge corpus

verified.how: opened and read in the browser pane
quotes: The harness is the architecture surrounding the model. How it renders context, executes actions, manages state, and decides when a task is done shapes outcomes just as much as the model itself.
Harness design alone can account for double-digit swings in benchmark results and significant differences in token cost, with the same underlying model.
Programmable loop engineering: Orchestration loops are ordinary Python, writable by developers and by the model itself.
A standard Python method whose body is an ellipsis is completed at runtime by an LLM-driven loop. Method with a normal body run as ordinary, deterministic Python.
verified.numbers: SWE-bench Verified, GPT-5.5: NOOA 82.2% at 29 LLM calls / ~1.1M tokens per task; comparison harnesses 78.2% at 66 calls / 2.2M tokens, and 78.6% at 29 calls / 1.3M tokens. Median session peaks 22-72k prompt tokens against a 200-400k window, so no compaction pass is needed.

nvidia-noaa-harness.caveat: NVIDIA's own engineering blog reporting NVIDIA's framework. The benchmark numbers are self-reported and the comparison harnesses are unnamed in the post. Read the technical report before quoting the delta as settled.

dsh-docs.title: DeepSeek Harness (dsh) — developer preview site and developer documentation
dsh-docs.author: DeepSeek
dsh-docs.audience: ICP2 first — a founder can read the plugin list and know exactly which pieces are hers to own; ICP1 second, as the vocabulary for arguing about a build-versus-adopt boundary in review
dsh-docs.ranking_criterion: it is the only source that ENUMERATES the harness rather than describing it: models, tools, skills, sessions, sandboxes, storage, loops, scheduling and the UI are named as separately swappable plugins, so 'what is the runtime' has a checkable answer instead of a metaphor
dsh-docs.acquisition: read in the browser 2026-08-26; not ingested into a cartridge corpus

verified.how: opened the preview site and the developer docs in the browser pane
quotes: The model is the soul of an agent. A harness lets an agent understand its environment, use tools, and keep working in real-world settings.
Plugins provide every agent capability, including models, tools, skills, sessions, sandboxes, storage, loops, scheduling, and the UI.
Everything the model sees is recorded in an append-only session log: system prompts, reasoning, tool calls and results, subagent scheduling, and every context injection.
verified.numbers: v0.1 developer preview, MIT licence. Four runtime modes: Standard, Code, Minimal (persistent bash + str_replace_editor only), Creator.

dsh-docs.caveat: DEVELOPER PREVIEW, and the project says so in capitals: compatibility-breaking changes are expected and the core plugins and APIs are still moving. Teach the ARCHITECTURE, which is the durable part; do not teach the API surface, which will not survive.

anthropic-long-running.title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
anthropic-long-running.author: Justin Young, Engineering at Anthropic
anthropic-long-running.audience: ICP2 — it is a field report on getting an agent to keep working across many context windows, which is the founder's actual problem; ICP1 will recognise the fix as a checklist the implementer may not edit
anthropic-long-running.ranking_criterion: it reports the failure that runs OPPOSITE to the one everyone expects. The agent does not run away; it looks around, sees progress, and declares the job done. A source that inverts the reader's prior earns its place ahead of one that confirms it.
anthropic-long-running.acquisition: read in the browser 2026-08-26; not ingested into a cartridge corpus

verified.how: opened and read in the browser pane
quotes: a later agent instance would look around, see that progress had been made, and declare the job done
It is unacceptable to remove or edit tests because this could lead to missing or buggy functionality.
Claude marks features as done prematurely.
verified.numbers: the claude.ai clone example expands one prompt into over 200 end-to-end features in a JSON file, all initially marked failing; coding agents may only flip the `passes` field.

anthropic-effective-agents.title: Building effective agents
anthropic-effective-agents.author: Engineering at Anthropic
anthropic-effective-agents.audience: both — it is the shared vocabulary. The workflow-versus-agent split is the phrasing ICP1 and ICP2 are both most likely to have already met, which makes it the cheapest common ground to argue from.
anthropic-effective-agents.ranking_criterion: it draws the boundary that the whole L1/L2 distinction rests on — predefined code paths versus the model directing its own process — and it is the boundary the other three sources each redraw differently
anthropic-effective-agents.acquisition: read in the browser 2026-08-26; not ingested into a cartridge corpus

verified.how: opened and read in the browser pane
quotes: Workflows are systems where LLMs and tools are orchestrated through predefined code paths.
Agents, on the other hand, are systems where LLMs dynamically direct their own processes and tool usage, maintaining control over how they accomplish tasks.
The task often terminates upon completion, but it's also common to include stopping conditions (such as a maximum number of iterations) to maintain control.
they often create extra layers of abstraction that can obscure the underlying prompts and responses, making them harder to debug

anthropic-effective-agents.caveat: STALE BY THE PUBLISHER'S OWN ADMISSION. The post carries a banner: much of the tooling landscape described has changed since December 2024. The DEFINITIONS are what is being cited here; the tooling list is not.

release-it-stability.title: Release It! — Stability Antipatterns and Stability Patterns (Timeouts, Circuit Breaker, Bulkheads, Fail Fast)
release-it-stability.author: Michael T. Nygard
release-it-stability.audience: ICP1 — this is the vocabulary a principal IC's reviewers already argue in. A founder can skip it; a principal IC who calls a retry storm anything other than a cascading failure will be corrected in review.
release-it-stability.ranking_criterion: it is the only source here that treats termination as a PROPERTY OF THE CALLER, arrived at from production incidents rather than from agent design, which is what lets the packet ask whether an agent loop is a new problem or an old one wearing new words
release-it-stability.acquisition: already ingested into the ic-principal-swe cartridge corpus as slice c01, digest-accepted (12 files, 186,429 words); DISK

verified.how: term-counted against the on-disk extracted text and the page index, not recalled
quotes: The timeout is a simple mechanism allowing you to stop waiting for an answer once you think it will not come.
verified.numbers: book.index.jsonl, 785 indexed pages. Densest content pages for the termination question: c01 pages 104-110 (Timeouts, then Circuit Breaker). Term counts across the corpus: timeout 108, circuit breaker 68, blocked thread 42, fail fast 32, bulkhead 26, unbounded/runaway 21. c02 pages 345-358 also match on these terms but are the BACK-OF-BOOK INDEX, not content, and are excluded.

release-it-stability.caveat: COPYRIGHTED BOOK TEXT. The extracted corpus stays local and is never committed to the public packet repo and never uploaded. What travels is the citation and the page range; the reader brings their own copy.
